active.title: The Spec Context Project stores no branch; context alive derives the checkout from the gitflow
active.description:
Measured (HEAD e83e55783): the registry field `current_branch` (`stored_branch` in `context show --json`) is read only by `alive()` DEAD->ALIVE (`features/spec_context/service.py:503-510`) and written by export (`features/export/service.py:58-59`), dead (`:756`) and alive (`:525`); it is stale in 3 of 5 ALIVE contexts of this instance (dadaia-workspace stores feature/0.4.6 while feature/0.5.0 is checked out; two consumer contexts lag the same way). `.dadaia/states/spec_contexts.json` stamps `schema_version: 2` while the store is `_VERSION = 3` (`infrastructure/json_context_store.py:20`) and never re-stamps; no JSON schema. Change (DELETE first): delete the field from `SpecContextProject` (`core/models/spec_context.py:43`; `RepoLiveStatus.current_branch`, the live read, stays), `_to_dict`/`_from_dict`, `context show/list` (`stored_branch` and the stored fallback, `cli/commands/context.py:80-81,275`; the live branch of an on-disk repo stays read from git), export, import and `features/migrate/state_v2.py:123`. `alive` derives the checkout: the highest `<gitflow.work><M.m.p>` on origin, else the integration branch, through the one gitflow reader (`GitSubprocessClient.gitflow`). The store re-stamps its `schema_version` on every write; a migration removes the key from existing rows. Done when: no reader or writer of the stored field remains (grep), and reviving a context whose origin holds `feature/0.5.0` lands on it. Files: core/models/spec_context.py, infrastructure/json_context_store.py, features/spec_context/service.py, cli/commands/context.py, features/export/service.py, features/import_/service.py, features/migrate/state_v2.py. Bugs eliminated: context-current-branch-stale-for-alive-repo, context-list-current-branch-stale-for-alive-repo. Same surface, not eliminated (the change must not grow it): sa-registry-schema-version-has-three-grammars and migrate-and-reconcile-crash-on-a-schema-3-context-registry (the 2-vs-3 stamp is their residue), registry-row-missing-a-key-escapes-reg-schema (open; the migration adds no second parse beside core/context_registry.py, ADR 0162). ADR 0171 (proposed).

active.title: Worktrees live at worktrees/<ctx>/<repo-slug>/<kind>-<M.m.p>-<letter>, kinds by repo role, one name parser
active.description:
Measured (HEAD e83e55783): `worktrees/<repo>/<M.m.p><letter>-<kind>` (`_NAME_RE`, `dd-gitflow-default/scripts/_worktree_kinds.py:32`) does not name the project; readers map a path to a context by repo-slug lookup or their own glob: the gate (`core/invocation.py:125-160`, `scope`/`repo_owner`), `dd-bug-resolution/scripts/_specs.py:44` (`*-{kind}`), doctor `check_worktrees` (filters by repo name), `hooks/ctx_inject.py:143-163`, the dead preflight and closure (`_release_phase.py:54-76`). `impl` reads the trio from the repo it opens in (`_worktree_new.py:35-43`), so an associated repo can never open `impl`; associated repos have no kind rule. Letter `_worktree_new.py:51-57`; version `_worktree_git.py:103-123` (`work_version`); `kind_for` (`_worktree_kinds.py:41`) has no production caller; ADRs 0097 and 0107 are both accepted for one shape. Change: `worktrees/<ctx>/<repo-slug>/<kind>-<M.m.p>-<letter>` on branch `wt/<kind>-<M.m.p>-<letter>`; `.gitkeep` in `worktrees/<ctx>/<repo-slug>/` created by context create/alive/repo add, removed by dead/repo remove; letter = lowest free per repo and version over all kinds; kinds by role (main `impl|bug|backlog|release`, associated `impl|bug`; `impl` in an associated repo reads the trio of the main repo); one name parser (`_NAME_RE`) through which every reader passes (gate `invocation.scope`, the `_specs.py` glob, doctor, ctx_inject, closure, `rows()`/`ours()`); delete `kind_for`. The worktrees/ path patterns of ADRs 0114, 0129 and 0132 read through the same parser. Migration: upgrade refuses while any worktree sits in the old layout (`fix:` merge or clean). Done when: a context with an associated repo opens `impl` and `bug` in both repos and the gate scopes both to the context. Files: dd-gitflow-default/scripts/_worktree_{kinds,new,git,end}.py, worktree.py, core/invocation.py, features/spec_context/gate_policy.py, dd-bug-resolution/scripts/_specs.py, features/spec_context/doctor.py, hooks/ctx_inject.py, dd-release-implementation/scripts/_release_phase.py, features/spec_context/service.py (create/alive/dead/repo add/remove), worktrees/AGENTS.md. active.title: context dead --snapshot pauses open worktrees: archive/wt tag for a private repo, local bundle for a public one
active.description:
Measured (HEAD e83e55783): `dead` refuses while any `wt/*` worktree of the context is open (`_dead_preflight`, `features/spec_context/service.py:679-692`, from `worktree_rows` and `GitSubprocessClient.unrecoverable`, `infrastructure/git_subprocess.py:244-266`; ADR 0128 layer 4), so work in flight cannot be paused; the exits are merge or clean only (ADRs 0099, 0128 layer 1); `alive` (`service.py:462-529`) knows nothing of worktrees. The pre-push already scans tags and skips branch policy for them (`features/chokepoints/push_gate.py:176-189`). Change: path 1 = merge (exists); path 2 = `context dead --snapshot`: an identity preflight (`GitSubprocessClient.identity_fix`) refuses before anything is touched -> per open `wt/*` a WIP commit on its branch that stages only that worktree (untracked included, ignored never; never `repos/<r>`) -> the same denylist+baseline scan the pre-push runs -> visibility by `gh repo view --json visibility` (unknown = public): private -> tag `archive/wt/<ctx>/<repo>/<name>` pushed to origin (never a branch, ADR 0120); public or unknown -> `git bundle` at `.dadaia/snapshots/<ctx>/<repo>/<name>.bundle` with a 'not portable' warning, in a new durable zone `.dadaia/snapshots/` (no TTL; a bundle leaves only when `alive` restores it or by an explicit verb; `export --hard` packs it from there; `.dadaia/reaped/` and the reaper gain no special case; ADR 0112, nothing is deleted by time) -> the worktree is removed. `alive` lists the context's snapshots and prints the restore `fix:` in the new layout. For `wt/*` trees the snapshot replaces the preflight's per-worktree refusal lines; a foreign worktree keeps its refusal. ADD justified: no unit carries pausing; it reuses the archive tag (ADR 0120), the push scan and `identity_fix`; its only new surface is the `snapshots` zone. Done when: dead with an open worktree in a public and in a private repo finishes losing no byte (the tag or the bundle restores the tree, untracked files included), and nothing of a public repo leaves the machine. Files: features/spec_context/service.py (dead, alive), infrastructure/git_subprocess.py (unrecoverable), features/chokepoints (scan, reused), dd-gitflow-default/scripts/_worktree_end.py, cli/commands/context.py, core/workspace_layout.py (the new `snapshots` zone in `DADAIA_ZONES`), public/data/dadaia-AGENTS.md (the zone row of `.dadaia/AGENTS.md`). Bugs (same mechanisms reused, must not regress): dead-commit-fails-without-git-identity (the WIP commit is the one commit dead still authors: identity preflight first), context-alive-sweeps-unrelated-worktree-changes (the WIP commit stages only the archived worktree), unrecoverable-fix-line-pushes-a-wt-branch-the-pre-push-refuses, sa-context-dead-removes-repos-outside-the-reaper, reaper-deletes-linked-git-worktrees. ADR 0173 (proposed; amends 0120 at acceptance).

Scope grill 2026-10-11 (operator, verbatim): 'vc está maluco de propor apagar??? ... fiquei horas e horas desenhando a solução, respondi grill-me, para criarmos a melhor solução de export e import ... perdeu tudo que fizemos porra?' (the whole replication block is restored as designed in the 2026-10-03 grill); layout: 'Contexto no path (Recommended)'. Earlier rulings kept: 2026-10-03 'Scan + público vai local (Recommended)'; 'Zona durável própria (Recommended)'. Destination: 0.5.0. Wave: 3 (a user feature, built on the clean Wave 2 base). Scope now: as designed above (ADR 0173): dead with an open worktree merges or snapshots it (tag for a private repo, a bundle in the durable snapshots zone for a public or unknown one); gh is optional and an absent or unknown answer counts as public; restore paths use the new layout.

active.description:

The doctor and ctx_inject use the same computation as `context show`; the doctor reports an orphan worktree (repo in no context, context DEAD). Zero state file (ADR 0108). ADD justified: no unit answers 'which worktrees does this project have'; the answer is derived, never stored, and `check_worktrees`' own repo-name filter is replaced by the shared computation instead of growing a second one. Done when: the same list comes out of `context show`, doctor and ctx_inject from one computation (ctx_inject already renders the doctor's, `hooks/ctx_inject.py:143-154`). active.title: dadaia export is read-only: soft (JSON, default) for the team, hard (tar.gz with bundles) to move a machine
active.description:
Measured (HEAD e83e55783): `dadaia export` (`features/export/service.py`) writes `.dadaia/dist/spec-contexts.json` (`spec-contexts-export-v1`) with contexts and the main repo's branch only, and rewrites the registry as a side effect (`_refresh_branches`, `:49-63`, `self._store.update` at `:59`); it knows no harness and no WIP; this instance's artifact dates from 0.4.5 (2026-09-04). Import (`features/import_/service.py:59-74`) raises `KeyError` on a record without name/slug/repo_url, uncaught by the CLI (`cli/commands/import_.py:34` catches DadaiaError/ValueError), and turns `repo_url: null` into the string 'None'. Scope narrowed by SPEC 0.4.6 D12/D15 (tar retired, f4bf7e0b2); no ADR covers export. Change: export is read-only (delete `_refresh_branches` and its `_store.update`); soft (default) `.dadaia/dist/spec-contexts.json` schema v2: contexts (slug, name, state, main repo url, associated [{slug,url}]), the exact `dadaia_version`, the harnesses of `.dadaia/states/harness_profile.json`, per repo its snapshots (tags portable; bundles listed as not portable, warning exit); hard `dadaia export --hard` -> one `.tar.gz` in `.dadaia/dist/` = soft + bundles of every open worktree and every bundle of `.dadaia/snapshots/`, content passed through the denylist+baseline scan (a hit refuses); never the denylist, credentials, sessions or the install ledger. The `dist` zone (`core/workspace_layout.py:194`) admits both. The artifact reader is hardened: an incomplete record -> DadaiaError, a null url refused. ADD justified: the hard artifact is the one carrier of local-only work (a public repo's bundle never leaves by git). It does not resurrect the retired tar pipeline's bug class (import-extracts-manifest-to-root): one archive of fixed members (the soft JSON and `snapshots/<ctx>/<repo>/<name>.bundle`); every member validated before extraction (no absolute path, no `..`, no link, nothing outside that list); the JSON is read in memory and extraction is confined to `.dadaia/snapshots/`, never the root. Done when: soft and hard validate against their schemas; a hard export with a planted secret is refused. Files: features/export/service.py, cli/commands/export.py, core/models/spec_context.py (EXPORT_SCHEMA_VERSION), core/workspace_layout.py (dist zone), the artifact reader, public/schemas (two new schemas). Bugs (class guarded): import-extracts-manifest-to-root (a restored archive lands outside its zone), import-export-workspace-flag-re-resolves-through-ancestor-walk (export half), context-create-admits-uncloneable-empty-url (the null-url class). ADR 0175 (proposed; supersedes SPEC 0.4.6 D12/D15 for the hard export).

Scope grill 2026-10-11 (operator, verbatim): 'vc está maluco de propor apagar??? ... fiquei horas e horas desenhando a solução, respondi grill-me, para criarmos a melhor solução de export e import ... perdeu tudo que fizemos porra?' Destination: 0.5.0. Wave: 3 (a user feature, built on the clean Wave 2 base). Scope now: complete as designed above (ADR 0175): export is read-only, soft JSON by default for the team, hard archive with bundles to move a machine.

active.title: init DIR --from <artifact> replicates a workspace at the artifact's exact version; dadaia import is deleted
active.description:
Measured (HEAD e83e55783): replicating is a manual three-step recipe (init, import, alive per context) with no version imposed; init never reads an export and re-packs the running distribution with no index (`infrastructure/python_env.py:318-360`), so a private index needs no code (`UV_INDEX_URL`/`PIP_INDEX_URL`). Change: `init DIR --from <artifact>` (soft or hard): a version other than the artifact's refuses with the exact `fix: uvx dadaia-workspace==<v> init DIR --from <file>`; installs the artifact's harnesses; registers its contexts DEAD through the one `register` (`SpecContextService.register`); checks access with `git ls-remote` and lists the unreachable repos; a hard artifact extracts its bundles, members validated, into `.dadaia/snapshots/<ctx>/<repo>/`, where `alive` restores them; prints `fix: context alive <ctx>` for each context ALIVE in the artifact. Delete `dadaia import` (`features/import_/`, `cli/commands/import_.py`, its `cli/main.py:27,68` registration): re-running init is the upgrade, so `--from` serves a new and an existing workspace. Docs: the atom `specs/memory/product/platform/context-portability.md` is rewritten with the three prerequisites (the export; PyPI or a private index via `UV_INDEX_URL`/`PIP_INDEX_URL` at the exact version; access to the listed GitHub repos). Done when: a clean container runs `init --from` on a soft and a hard artifact -> `context alive` -> doctor with no finding. Files: cli/commands/init.py, infrastructure/python_env.py, features/import_/ (deleted), cli/commands/import_.py (deleted), cli/main.py, container.py, specs/memory/product/platform/context-portability.md. Bugs eliminated (the verb is gone): import-registers-unvalidated-slugs-that-doctor-fix-inv5-rmtrees, import-export-workspace-flag-re-resolves-through-ancestor-walk (import half). Same surface, not eliminated: init-on-a-copied-workspace-leaves-a-cli-bound-to-the-original (open; `--from` becomes the supported path instead of copying, the copy defect stays), r3b-portability-import-venv-permission. active.title: ARCHITECTURE.md's ADR section is generated from the ledger; the P-NN ADR label and the pairing law leave
active.description:
Measured (HEAD c9100eaee): 8 of 147 accepted ADRs are cited anywhere in `specs/memory` (0015, 0021, 0023, 0025, 0119, 0138, 0143, 0167); 5 principle labels cite rejected ADRs as accepted (`ARCHITECTURE.md:13` P-01->0001, `:43` P-09->0003, `:68` P-14->0004, `:73` P-15->0004; `QUALITY.md:33` P-29->0012); 10 principles say `ADR: none`; no doctor check compares labels to ledger status (`features/specs/doctor_adr.py:49-80` flags only superseded ids); the label patch 9cfea65cd was reverted by 83b7bc52f - a symptom fix on a structure that duplicates ledger status in prose. Change: one generated block in ARCHITECTURE.md listing every accepted, non-superseded ADR (id, title, one-line decision), rendered from `decisions.jsonl` through the existing `core/fixed_sections.py` marker mechanism (a ledger-rendered variant); doctor FIXED-2 (`features/specs/doctor_memory.py:119-146`) on diff, `--fix` regenerates; the block is exempt from MEM-NARRATIVE-1 (`features/specs/memory_lint.py:72-108`). The closure memory pass regenerates it, and the regeneration refuses an accepted ADR whose measured_by does not resolve to an existing pytest node id or doctor code (a promise is allowed until then); the release names the accepted forms (test paths and node ids, doctor codes, lint contracts and CI jobs per `specs/memory/AGENTS.md:21`) and keeps the regression seam of sa-adr-measured-by-pattern-refuses-real-checks as the guard. DELETE: the `ADR:` label on `### P-NN` principles and its parser `memory_lint.py:84` `_ADR_LINE_RE`; the pairing law (`specs/ADRs/AGENTS.md:28` accept row's "paired canonical-memory hunk", §5 :46, §5.1 :48-53; `specs/memory/AGENTS.md:11` and the `ADR:` clause of :21); the pillar-3 pairing check (the pairing clause of `dd-audit-project/PILLAR-MEMORY.md:9` and :18-19 - its missing-`Measured by:` finding stays); their scaffold mirrors (`scaffold/ADRs/AGENTS.md:43-51`, the `ADR:` clause of `scaffold/memory/AGENTS.md:21`). A principle stands on its `Measured by:`. Done when: ARCHITECTURE.md's ADR block equals the projection; no `ADR:` label grammar remains; the 5 drifts are gone by construction. Relates: adr-born-at-release-with-options, adr-ledger-triage-process-rules. Bugs: adr-measured-by-existence-unchecked (being registered) delivers the existence check this reuses; prior sa-adr-measured-by-pattern-refuses-real-checks.

Scope grill 2026-10-11 (operator, verbatim): 'Triagem + gerada (Recommended)'. Earlier rulings kept: 2026-10-03 'ARCHITECTURE.md seja a foto final do ledger ... sessão dedicada e atualizada das ADRs'; 'limiar deve aumentar, criterio Azure'; 'Gerada do ledger'; 'Triagem única'; 'Real no closure'. Tension noted: 2026-10-08 'desidratar ... Memory referencia a implementação, não repete'. Destination: 0.5.0. Wave: 1 and 4 (Wave 1: the status token leaves the `ADR:` grammar, since ledger status is law the agents read; Wave 4: the triage and the generated section, after the ledger is final). Scope now: Wave 1 deletes the `ADR:` status label grammar, so status lives only in the ledger. Wave 4 runs the one-time triage (process rules and spent rulings superseded by their law line; survivors get a real measured_by per 'Real no closure', superseded records do not count) and generates the ARCHITECTURE.md ADR section from the ledger, one line (id and title) per survivor, with the doctor FIXED check.

active.title: Existing code migrates to the multi-platform-by-construction ADR, rules P1-P10, one sweep per rule
active.description:
Operator, 2026-10-07, verbatim: 'toda arquitetura e a forma como metodos são programados deve pensar em ser multi-plataforma'; 'tanto na lib, na CLI, nos scripts dentro de skills'; ADR accepted the same day: 'Aceito, com essa divisão (Recommended)'. The ADR has no id yet: decisions.jsonl on feature/0.5.0 and every rc-10 tree carries no multi-platform record (the rc-10 Reconciliation writes it through its lane). Decision: one codebase; OS facts live in one seam, dadaia_workspace/core/platform.py, and tooling refuses OS literals elsewhere. Rules: P1 platform.py is the only reader of sys.platform/os.name, venv dir and .exe via sysconfig; P2 never bare python/bash - sys.executable, executables via shutil.which; P3 list argv, shell=False, no shlex; P4 pathlib in code, as_posix only for display/compare, no '/' joins; P5 encoding='utf-8' on all text I/O incl. hook stdout, CI never masks with PYTHONUTF8; P6 rmtree onexc read-only handler, os.replace atomic writes, no exec bit/symlink reliance; P7 one renderer for printed commands (core/cli_line), never &&, $VAR, sudo, chmod +x; P8 git and harness hooks are a one-line #!/bin/sh shim exec'ing the absolute interpreter, logic in Python; P9 shipped law names commands once, neutral, rendered per platform at install; P10 ruff PTH, S602, S605, PLW1514, a guard refusing OS literals outside the seam, Windows+macOS CI = Linux selection, .gitattributes eol. Split (ruled): rc-10 bug batch takes the 8 Windows bugs, shipped-law-hardcodes-the-posix-venv-path (P9) and CI selection parity (P10 CI part); this entry is the rc-11 rest - hook shims (P8), pre-push in Python, lint + guard (P10), path joins (P4), one command renderer (P7). Design: one sweep per P-rule over dadaia_workspace/ (lib, CLI, skill scripts), each sweep lands with its repo guard (the P10 OS-literal guard or the named ruff rule) turned on in the same job so the rule cannot regress; each sweep's commit carries its git grep line and hit count. Open (to the PLAN): how skill scripts get command lines without a second decider - relay the CLI's rendered output. Placement rc-11 is the operator's split; every other design detail not quoted from a ruling is agent default, unruled.

Scope grill 2026-10-11 (operator, verbatim): 'Tudo, P8 relativo (Recommended)'. Earlier rulings kept: 2026-10-07 'windows deve satisfazer as mesmas necessidades que linux ... toda arquitetura ... multi-plataforma. porra'; 'tanto na lib, na CLI, nos scripts dentro de skills'; ADR 0220 'Aceito, com essa divisão (Recommended)'. Destination: 0.5.0. Wave: 3 (platform sweep over the clean Wave 2 base). The release skill uses `drift.report` (`_release_tree.py:267`, `release.py:135`), `drift.render` (`release.py:136`), `drift.git` (`_release_tree.py:218,272`, `release.py:146`) and `drift.Refusal` (`_release_tree.py:220`, `release.py:156,281`). `tests/infrastructure/test_public_assets__public_scripts_thin_wrapper.py` still allows exactly that edge in `_CROSS_SKILL_EDGES` (:56) and `_EDGE_PATH_LINES` (:61). rc-14 PLAN 1.5 planned its DELETE in Job 12; the Job 12 ruling carried it (8be8949d7), because `memory.py drift` takes only `--since`, `--json` and `--specs`. Design, one of two: (a) the release skill runs `memory.py drift` through the sibling script path; the verb gains `--until`, and its JSON carries the fields the release skill reads today (the git lookup, the rendered worklist, the refusal); or (b) the worklist decider moves into the kernel (`dd-bug-resolution/scripts`) and both skills call it. Relation: residual of skill-scripts-one-kernel, which exits with rc-14 and would otherwise trace this row as done. Done when: no `sys.path` line in the release skill reaches another skill, `_CROSS_SKILL_EDGES` and `_EDGE_PATH_LINES` are deleted with their comment, and the thin-wrapper test is green. Placement: unruled.

active.title: The one-owner residue the rc-14 G1 readout measured: git runners, bare os.replace, ledger-store commit loops, an inline fix line
active.description: ADR 0246 gives every shared fact one owner; the rc-14 closure G1 readout (PLAN.md '### Closure readouts', 5dc5f1166, 64b3b3b85) left these sites outside their owner. D1: 11 subprocess hits beside the kernel's _git.git, in _backlog_exit.py, _specs.py, bugs.py, registry.py, verdict.py, _release_phase.py, _worktree_end.py (two), _worktree_git.py and infrastructure/git_subprocess.py; a call that runs another component's script or a non-git tool may stay, a git call goes through _git. D2: features/spec_context/sweep.py:242 and features/workspace/service.py:108 still call os.replace beside the one atomic writer _atomic.py (a cross-device move and a staged rename: keep each with its reason, or route it through the owner). D7-D9: the three ledger stores still define their own commit (_backlog_store.py:46, _bugs_store.py:49, _release_store.py:94) and the backlog and bug checks their own finding helpers (_backlog_check.py:83, _bugs_check.py:140) beside _commit.py, _jsonl.py and _findings.py. Fix line: cli/commands/specs.py:94 spells an inline 'fix:' line outside the raisers. D4 (verdict.py:22 context pattern) is the open bug verdict-context-pattern-disagrees-with-core and is not in this entry. Design: the as-is review gives each site DELETE or KEEP-with-reason by the deletion test; no new owner, no flag. Next candidate. Agent default, unruled: one grouped entry, since the items share ADR 0246's design.
